findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking by a user with no destination calendar (handleNewBooking:1067 sets `null`) throws TypeError and the entire booking request 500s.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Video references are now written with `credentialId: undefined`, so reschedule/cancel paths gated on `reference.credentialId` (handleNewBooking:1107, handleCancelBooking:491) silently skip deleting the old Zoom/video meeting.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — For a destination calendar row with a null credentialId the fan-out calls createEvent without an externalId while GoogleCalendarService resolves the target by credentialId match, so the event lands in "primary" and the reference records externalCalendarId undefined - a write that "succeeds" into the wrong calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credentials are fetched by raw id from the DB with no ownership or app-enabled check, bypassing getApps validation used in the constructor, so a destination calendar pointing at another user's or a globally disabled app's credential is still used to write events.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — On merge (newBookingId) only the first old calendar reference is deleted via `.find`, so the other hosts' old calendar events are orphaned after reschedule-into-existing-booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:290 — BOOKING_CANCELLED webhook body spreads `evt`, so subscribers' `payload.destinationCalendar` silently changes from object/null to an array with no version bump.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:356 — BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payload's `destinationCalendar` becomes an array (e2e expectation flipped null -> [] at apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249), an unversioned public webhook shape change.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:267 — Reschedule-request webhook body spreads `evt`, changing `destinationCalendar` from object/null to array for external subscribers.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — Calendar.createEvent` gains a `credentialId` param but office365 (:72), lark (:125) and BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125) still ignore it and use `destinationCalendar[0]`, so the new multi-destination contract is unfulfilled for every non-Google adapter.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking by a user with no destination calendar (handleNewBooking:1067 sets `null`) throws TypeError and the entire booking request 500s.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Video references are now written with `credentialId: undefined`, so reschedule/cancel paths gated on `reference.credentialId` (handleNewBooking:1107, handleCancelBooking:491) silently skip deleting the old Zoom/video meeting.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — For a destination calendar row with a null credentialId the fan-out calls createEvent without an externalId while GoogleCalendarService resolves the target by credentialId match, so the event lands in "primary" and the reference records externalCalendarId undefined - a write that "succeeds" into the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (around the new loop), when a destination calendar entry has no credentialId, the code fans out over credentials matching destination.integration but calls createEvent(c, event) without passing destination.externalId. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards only credential.id to calendar.createEvent, and GoogleCalendarService.createEvent selects the calendarId via calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId, defaulting to "primary" when not found. For a destination row with null credentialId, no match is possible, so Google inserts into "primary" and the returned EventResult.externalId is undefined, which later becomes externalCalendarId in references (EventManager uses result.externalId). This is a concrete behavior change that can silently create the event in the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credentials are fetched by raw id from the DB with no ownership or app-enabled check, bypassing getApps validation used in the constructor, so a destination calendar pointing at another user's or a globally disabled app's credential is still used to write events.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts inside createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination calendar includes destination.credentialId, the code first tries this.calendarCredentials, but if not found it falls back to prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } }) and then uses that credential to call createEvent. This DB lookup is by raw id only and does not constrain by userId/teamId/ownership or any “enabled/allowed app” filtering; it reconstructs a CredentialWithAppName solely from the fetched row. That means a crafted/incorrect destination.credentialId could cause EventManager to write events using a credential that wasn’t part of the prevalidated this.calendarCredentials set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — On merge (newBookingId) only the first old calendar reference is deleted via `.find`, so the other hosts' old calendar events are orphaned after reschedule-into-existing-booking.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the code was updated to treat calendar references as an array (using `.filter(...)` and looping over all `_calendar` references), implying multiple calendar references can exist per booking. However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId)`), it still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which selects only one old calendar reference to delete. If there are multiple old calendar references, the remaining ones will not be deleted, leaving orphaned external calendar events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:290 — BOOKING_CANCELLED webhook body spreads `evt`, so subscribers' `payload.destinationCalendar` silently changes from object/null to an array with no version bump.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` (see `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`). In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the constructed `evt` now always sets `destinationCalendar` to an array (`[bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar]`, `[user.destinationCalendar]`, or `[]`) instead of the prior object/null shape. The webhook E2E fixture is also updated from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, confirming an externally visible payload shape change. Whether there is (or should be) a version bump isn’t shown in the diff, but the breaking contract change itself is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose destinationCalendar is null/[] throws a TypeError

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the new logic does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ??
